findings.claim: Hackathon publishes NO metric: zero hits for CER, WER, metric, S/D/I, seconds, latency, score, weight; evaluation table 2 cols x 6 rows, no weights; product-weighted (innovation, business use case, feasibility, roadmap, team, market).
No official deadline: 10 of 12 timeline rows TBD; only launch 12/02/2026 and Pitch Screening 23/07/2026 dated. 'Qualifiers 30/09' belongs to RAJASTHAN hackathon; Oct 4 / Oct 15 unsourced.
'22 languages' appears nowhere on official page; baselines named: Tesseract, EasyOCR, TrOCR, PaddleOCR; architectures LayoutLM/Donut/DocTR. 22-language scope is ours, not mandated.

Problem statement asks for layout-preserving JSON + searchable PDF; organiser contact gic.dibd@gmail.com; Evaluation/Eligibility tabs did not render for fetcher so Gate 1 licensing cannot close from public pages alone.

Sarvam 87.39 is macro-average over 22 non-English languages (our arithmetic 87.3909) on 6,909 block-level samples (6,609 excl. 300 English); card defines Word Accuracy=100x(1-WER) but never states 87.39 IS that; not comparable to any CER of ours.

Sarvam bench: GT 'reviewed twice by human language experts'; runaway-repetition and ambiguous-GT samples excluded; block-level vs our page-level (1,227 pages); degenerate outputs dropped by them, scored 1.0 by us.
Sarvam and Bodhan vendor benches disagree on per-language winners on 8 of 22 languages; Kashmiri flips by 8.9 points; neither is third-party arbiter.

Gate 1 Bodhan base CONDITIONAL PASS: sample-100 (n=99) 4-bit CER 0.6878 vs bf16 0.6863 (delta 0.0015, B-01 PASS); pair-only 300 gold 0.4034 vs 0.4010, beats surya 0.5660; bench small_rep n=1173 CER 0.0540 WER 0.1356, 0.52 s/crop; official-path parity waits GPU day.
Bodhan variants on disk (level2/models_bodhan): official 1.8 GB, MLX 4-bit 633 MB, MLX bf16 1.7 GB, all Apache-2.0.

Plan v3 flowchart: only wrap-and-route path BUILT (10 local engines, per-script router); preprocess (OpenCV), layout (DocLayout-YOLO / PP-DocLayoutV3 / Bodhan 33M), TrOCR+Qwen-VL+PaddleOCR-VL SFT with akshara-aux loss, schema head SimPO/DPO all SPEC-ONLY; all training PAUSED.

W6 QLoRA scope = Konkani ONLY: Punjabi K1 is a TIE (90 common items, 87 ties, 3 discordant, p=1.00); Konkani passes (31 discordant, p=0.0033, 19.4pt vs easyocr p=0.0107 n=100; 22.0pt vs tesseract-family). mai+or KILLED at K1. KILL_CRITERIA.md:56 superseded by erratum.
McNemar exact per-item pass/fail where pass = CER<0.5 (cer_threshold 0.5), two-sided; ~90 ties/language gives little power.

22-language labelled = 1,683 (probe22 1,283 + South 400); scored probe22 1,227 (12,324 rows, 10 engines/11 model strings) + South 126/400; n>=50 in 13 of 22; Malayalam n=5 below 5-10 floor; smallest other n: Assamese 19, mni 20, sat 20, gu 24, kn 25, te 26, doi 27, ne 37.
Three Tesseract aliases not byte-identical: predictions differ on 857 of 1,227 items.

Best local engine at n>=50: surya 9, tesseract-family 2, easyocr 1. Winner CERs worst-first: ur 0.623, ks 0.589, bn 0.476, kok 0.425, sd 0.316, or 0.259, hi 0.220, mr 0.205, sa 0.175, brx 0.165, pa 0.145, mai 0.030. Largest gap: Hindi 0.220 vs 0.504 (28.4pt); Konkani 0.4248 vs 0.6186 (19.4pt).

Sarvam vs local by GT tier (54 paired items): official_pair_txt human gold bn/hi/sa n=9 Sarvam 0.064 vs surya 0.535 vs best-local oracle 0.243; official_pdf_layer n=36 Sarvam 0.311 / surya 0.229; sarvam_bench n=9 Sarvam 0.278 / surya 0.730 / oracle 0.617.

On 18 human-verified items Sarvam CER 2.5x lower than best-of-10 local oracle (0.171 vs 0.430); vs surya-always 3.70x (0.171 vs 0.632); excluding mni/sat 2.02x (0.132 vs 0.265) -> a third is coverage gap. All 21 local item-level wins over Sarvam are in PDF-layer tier, none human-verified; PDF-layer GT may be an artefact.

sheet.csv stored CER column does not re-derive (111/400 sampled rows within 1e-4, 66 exact; later: 62.9% of 12,324 cells), yet every headline survives independent recomputation (same winner in all 12 n>=50 langs; surya<Sarvam 10/18; item-level 21/28/5; Konkani 0.4248->0.4286). Adopt sheet_v2.csv (U9).
'10/18 vs 8/18' conflict was methodological (same 3 items per language vs surya full-language mean vs Sarvam's 3).
South scored only 126 of 400 (219 nulled gt_thin at GT<200 chars, 55 nulled mojibake); dominant-script partition kn and ml ~4 scored pages each; lang-tag kn=25, ml=5.
Probe corpus coverage gap: all 1,283 items printed, 0 tables, 0 mixed-script, quality unknown for 983; handwriting/degraded/low-quality never measured though hackathon targets them (U13).
Weakest cells named: Santali and Meetei Mayek (no local engine emits script), Nastaliq cursive (ur, ks), degraded scans untested.
0 of 200 local-engine predictions on Santali contain a single Ol Chiki char; no local engine reads Ol Chiki or Meetei Mayek; level2/probe22/tessdata lacks only mni and sat.

indic-ocr tessdata Apache-2.0 (blob 8dada3e), includes Ol Chiki and Meetei Mayek: sat.traineddata 1,546,915 B, mni.traineddata 2,843,488 B; lives in sibling indic-ocr/tessdata repo. U7 licence-cleared; supersedes proto-83 all-rights-reserved. Download decided YES after licence check.
Bodhan card scores surya OCR 2 at 0.1 on both Manipuri and Santhali (Gemini 0.8/0.2): surya cannot serve mni/sat; only Apache indic-ocr backstop candidate.
Script identifier (anikde/STscriptdetect, MIT) is ViT-base-patch16-224-in21k, not CLIP; its 12 classes contain no sat and no mni -> routing cannot cover the two dead languages.
Fonts: machine has 1 Ol Chiki and 10 Meetei Mayek fonts; GlotOCR paper attributes low-tier failure to pretraining coverage not font availability (median 1 font per family, unverified from full text).
mni/sat BARRED verdict may be verifier-competence artefact: GT from sarvam_bench, human-reviewed twice, not machine GT; re-verify with a human (U6); section 6.4 stays LOCKED.
No literature baseline for sat/mni/or page OCR: Ol Chiki digits only (99.13% digit set); Meitei Mayek NO OCR paper; Odia char-level only. Kashmiri Nastaliq: no CER paper.
Best published hard-case CERs: Urdu printed Nastaliq 0.91% (Nasir 2024); Urdu handwritten 5.27% (Hamza 2024); Hindi handwritten 2.14% (Kumar 2026); degraded Sanskrit print 3.71% (Dwivedi 2020).

ICDAR 2023 Indic HTR winner 95.94% CRR / 88.31% WRR (Mondal 2023); PARSeq-style transfer printed->handwritten strongest across 10 Indic languages (Lalitha 2025); SemiHastakshar, PLATTER page-level HTR; 'Handwriting is now central' (proto-104 rev3 section H), triggers RQ-10.
NOTE: ICDAR'23 figure here 88.31 WRR conflicts with Plan v4's 96.10 WRR Bengali best (different language/metric?); not reconciled in these files.

Fusion ceiling: oracle over 10 engines 0.3213 vs surya-always 0.4190 (gap 0.098) on 300 seeded items, but 67% of gap is `sa` where surya emits 100% empty (bug); ex-sa gap 0.0332. Original 0.4277/0.5229 withdrawn.

All four edge theses killed (12 critiques): akshara-validity fusion verifier 61% worse than surya (0.6766 vs 0.4190); script-mismatch router 95-100% precision, 0-5% recall, routing gain -0.0351 CER; per-script-block metric already in Sarvam; GT purity gate was a bug. Zero edge survived.
Multi-engine voting: full ensemble beat all singles on 0 of 115 pages (B12); fusion = agreement flag only; raw confidence unreliable proxy (Jhala 2026).

Adaptive engine selection +23.7% over single engines on 15k govt docs (Zhang 2026); selection != voting; RQ-11 oracle gap decides whether router worth building. Consensus-entropy OCR (CVPR 2026) already publishes training-free routing.

Engine speed from 13,289 packs: surya 24.3 s/page (~36 h for 5,344; p90 72 s ~107 h); indicphotoocr 17.1 s (~25 h); paddleocr 11.4 s (~17 h); easyocr 11.1 s (~16 h); tesseract-family 2.6 s (~3.8 h); rapidocr 0.40 s (~0.6 h).

Abstention (empty prediction = CER 1.0): anuvaad 59.4%, paddleocr 56.1%, rapidocr 39.7%, surya 17.4%, tesseract-family 8.2-8.4%, easyocr 3.3%. (Plan draft earlier said paddleocr_indic 43.7% to anuvaad 50.3%.)

Bootstrap 95% CI (10k, seed 20260926): brx 0.166 [0.106,0.234] overlaps hi 0.222 [0.191,0.255]; kok 0.428 [0.389,0.468] vs ur 0.628 [0.616,0.640] non-overlap; only non-overlapping gaps defensible. Metric set should add median + catastrophic-failure rate (CER>0.5) + NFC statement.
NFC vs NFKC differs on 564/12,324 strings with 0 exact-match flips: not worth time.

LICENCE surya: code Apache-2.0 but weights OpenRAIL-M modified; sec 2(c) forbids product competing with Licensor, no carve-out; sec 8 share-alike extends to Output/derivatives; NOT CLEARED commercially (U14 reframed; $5M cap not blocker). Training on surya output inherits sec 8.

Kashmiri 600K dataset NOT commercially cleared (card CC-BY-4.0 but embeds Controlled Research Access License); B-03 stays HOLD; Koshur Pixel (2606.23144) and synthocr-gen (2601.16113) licence check pending.

Bodhan licence: no attribution in OCR output (UI/docs notice only); hosting needs prior written approval (3.1); internal-component carve-out 3.2; 90-day open-release waiver; no relicensing; anything 'trained substantially on Output' is Derivative. Submission shaped as internal component.
EasyOCR code MIT (NAVER) but weight .pth is JaidedAI release asset: weight licence OPEN.
Free-tier VLM APIs must not produce GT (Gemini etc.); VLM layout annotation superseded by Bodhan IndicDocLayout; Sep 10 sync '100/lang' attribution wrong (20-sample sets).

Day-2 leak-free rule: a writer/page never in both train and eval; split by source document, hold out 10% of documents per language; Sarvam bn/hi/sa + Korean 300 gold pairs = external test never trained on.
Consensus: OCR-specialised base + LoRA beats generic VLM; same-language pretraining 92% WRR vs cross-lingual 51% vs scratch 6% (Chitrapathak-2 Faraz 2026; Manna 2025).

4-bit LoRA often preserves gains (6/10): QARI 4-bit; Elkousy 4-bit Qwen2.5-VL -29% CER Arabic. Contradicts proto-100 B-01 (no 4-bit for ks/ur/sd; QARI 3.45 vs 0.091); Day-1 measured 4-bit vs bf16 per script decides.

Synthetic necessary but insufficient: Baseer 300k synthetic + 200k real; clean renders look tied, real scans collapse 9/10 systems (EasyOCR chrF++ 93.6 -> 58.3, Singh 2026). Data volume: 100-1,000 lines aid transfer; full OCR needs hundreds of lines or thousands of word images.
RLVR/GRPO moderate 4/10 (keep last/optional); hard-example mining weak 2/10 (do not build); label cleaning improves CER up to 1.8 pts (run proto-65 GT-defect checks before training).

LM post-OCR correction strong 8/10: CER hi 10.20->6.73, gu 6.10->1.39, mr 8.19->3.29; Sanskrit +23 pts; RoundTripOCR synthetic pairs hi/mr/ne/kok/brx/sa; corrector did not transfer across engines. Build candidate B-18 trained on Bodhan's own errors, leak-free, paired bootstrap, Day-4.

Restoration: PreP-OCR -63.9% to -70.3% relative CER on 13,831 real historical pages (measured only Latin-script); super-resolution helped low-res but HURT high-res (Rawat 2021). B-06 gated pre-pass only for low-quality inputs, A/B on degraded subset (RQ-6).

Layout+reading order strong 8/10 (IndicDLP 2512.20236, dots.ocr 2512.02498); IndicLID per-block language on recognised text (RQ-8); structured output schema B-11; Parichay 89.8% exact-match fields; competitors to add: Chitrapathak-2, LightOnOCR-2-1B, HunyuanOCR-1.5, GlotOCR Bench, Qwen3-VL-8B beat GPT-5.5 on real Devanagari scans.

Plan v3 backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B @4-bit locked PRIMARY (W6_QLORA_SPEC.md:53), GLM-OCR 0.9B alternate; no weights on disk then; GLM-OCR OmniDocBench v1.6 presence contradictory (94.71 rank 3 vs omitted). Plan v4 instead uses Bodhan.
